Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Mints

Mint gathering was remembered as shared work, guided by its scent and flowers. The catalogue records flavoring, aromatic, and ceremonial uses and concern that construction or spraying may have reduced familiar patches. It lists wild mint alongside other plants of the mint family.1

Places named in the catalogue

Shinnecock territories; Long Island.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF pp. 22–23. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
